title: Neutron Radiation Hardness of MAPD-3NM-I Silicon Photomultipliers with Deep-Buried Pixels
content: Neutron irradiation can degrade the performance of silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) used in radiation detection. This study investigates the neutron radiation hardness of MAPD-3NM-I SiPMs with deep-buried pixels, using surface-pixel MPPC-S12572-10P devices for comparison. The devices were exposed to mixed neutron--gamma fields at total neutron fluences of \(10^{10}\)--\(10^{13}\,\mathrm{n/cm^2}\). Dark current, breakdown voltage, capacitance, photosignal amplitude, and energy resolution were evaluated before and after irradiation, and dark-current recovery was monitored for 100 days. At \(10^{13}\,\mathrm{n/cm^2}\), the dark-current increase factors at 1 V overvoltage were \((5538\pm188)\) for MAPD and \((59111\pm2006)\) for MPPC. The remaining photosignal amplitudes were \((17.83\pm0.74)\%\) for MAPD at 1 V and \((3.84\pm0.15)\%\) for MPPC at 4.5 V. Breakdown-voltage shifts were approximately 0.8--0.9 V, whereas capacitance changes at 40 V were small relative to estimated uncertainties. Dark current partially recovered during room-temperature storage, with the largest changes observed between days 2 and 35. Under the investigated conditions, MAPD-3NM-I devices exhibited smaller degradation in several measured parameters, although larger device populations and matched operating conditions are needed to establish architecture-level differences.
